Reviewer view: the judge's full reasoning

This was an advance (scheduled) booking, and the cancellation fell outside the chargeable window. The trip record (EV-TRIP-02738) shows the booking accepted at 17:10:08 on 10 Aug 2026 for a scheduled pickup at 17:55:08, and the rider cancelled at 17:35:08 — 1,200 seconds before the scheduled time. The policy in force for this trip sets the advance cancellation grace at 900 seconds before the scheduled pickup (platform_policy.advance_grace_before_scheduled_sec), so the free-cancellation period ran up to 17:40:08. The rider cancelled more than 900 seconds before the scheduled time, and POL-NS-10(b) states that such a cancellation 'is not chargeable'. The trip was accepted at 17:10:08, well before that 900-second window opened, so POL-NS-10(b)'s proviso pulling limb (a) in from accepted_at does not apply, and the 180-second post-match grace of limb (a) is irrelevant. POL-NS-10(c) then directs that the fee charged on a cancellation made non-chargeable by limb (a) or (b) is refunded in full with no driver compensation: the payments ledger (EV-FARE-02738) shows cancellation_fee 4.50 SGD, total_charged 4.50 SGD, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the whole contested 4.50 SGD returns to the rider. To the driver: your reading of POL-NS-10(f) as the governing charging rule is rejected. Limb (f) charges 'a rider's own cancellation after the grace in limb (a) or (b)' — that is, one falling after the free-cancellation period has run. This cancellation was made inside the limb (b) advance grace (17:35:08, before the window opened at 17:40:08), so limb (f) is not engaged and limb (b) governs. Your remaining points are accepted as correct on the record but do not change the outcome: the driver did begin navigating 8 seconds after acceptance (17:10:16), the trace runs 157 fixes with no gaps and 100% coverage, no limb (f) refund exception is made out, and the 4.50 SGD fare line reconciles to the platform's published figure, so no POL-NS-08(d) defect arises. To the rider: your core case is right, and it is independently supported. The baseline no-show charge also fails: POL-NS-01 limb (a) requires a driver 'arrived' event in the trip record and there is none (arrived_at is null and the event list runs driver_assigned to driver_en_route to trip_cancelled only), and limb (d) requires termination under RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT, whereas the record closes with RIDER_CANCELLED. The driver's own trace places him about 14,000 m from the pickup pin and moving at 57–63 km/h at the moment of cancellation, so the 180-second free waiting period was never served (0 seconds of in-geofence dwell) and POL-NS-06 supports a full refund. No driver compensation is payable: POL-NS-01 is not satisfied on any limb, so POL-NS-07's payout condition is never reached, and the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip (no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the required 4, and 2/90 = 0.022, below the required 0.08), so POL-NS-09(d) is not engaged. Evidence quality: the ruling rests on the trip record and the fare breakdown, both carrying weight_multiplier 1.0, and no POL-NS-08 limb is engaged (no clock skew, no trace gap over 120 seconds, the chat log is internally consistent, and the fare line reconciles), so confidence is not capped below 1.0 and is stated at 0.92. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02738-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; it carries no fact this ruling needs (POL-NS-06(i) accumulation is not required) and it does not affect the outcome or the confidence. No clause produces a referral and the case does not escalate: confidence 0.92 is above the 0.70 floor. The monetary effect of 4.50 SGD is at or below the 8.00 SGD execution threshold, so this provisional ruling is executed automatically on issue.

How to appeal: You may appeal once within 30 days (POL-GEN-04). A different human reviewer hears it, and only record evidence may be added.

POL-GEN-05: the monetary effect is SGD 4.50 against an execution threshold of SGD 8.00. It does not exceed the threshold, so the amount is executed automatically on issue, subject to POL-GEN-04.

Read POL-GEN-04 in full
Every ruling issued without human review is a provisional ruling. Either party may appeal it once, within 30 days of the trip or of the ruling's issue, whichever is later, by lodging the appeal with the platform's help channel. An appeal (a) is heard by a human reviewer who did not take part in any earlier review of the same trip; (b) may add only record-type evidence - a GPS export, a fare or payment statement, an ERP gantry record with gantry name, entry time and cashcard statement, a call log, a photograph with its capture time - and may not add or amend a party statement; (c) suspends execution of any amount not yet executed and freezes it until decided, and where the amount was executed under POL-GEN-05 before the appeal, a successful appeal reverses it; (d) may not be withdrawn and re-lodged. A second appeal on the same trip, an appeal lodged after 30 days, or an appeal that adds only statements is refused. The appeal decision is recorded as a human closure under POL-GEN-06, enters the precedent store, and is final on the platform. This clause licenses no ruling value: an appeal is a route to human review, not a ruling, and it is lodged after a ruling has issued.

Draft 1 - sampled
This was an advance (scheduled) booking, and the cancellation fell outside the chargeable window. The trip record (EV-TRIP-02738) shows the booking accepted at 17:10:08 on 10 Aug 2026 for a scheduled pickup at 17:55:08, and the rider cancelled at 17:35:08 — 1,200 seconds before the scheduled time. The policy in force for this trip sets the advance cancellation grace at 900 seconds before the scheduled pickup (platform_policy.advance_grace_before_scheduled_sec), so the free-cancellation period ran up to 17:40:08. The rider cancelled more than 900 seconds before the scheduled time, and POL-NS-10(b) states that such a cancellation 'is not chargeable'. The trip was accepted at 17:10:08, well before that 900-second window opened, so POL-NS-10(b)'s proviso pulling limb (a) in from accepted_at does not apply, and the 180-second post-match grace of limb (a) is irrelevant. POL-NS-10(c) then directs that the fee charged on a cancellation made non-chargeable by limb (a) or (b) is refunded in full with no driver compensation: the payments ledger (EV-FARE-02738) shows cancellation_fee 4.50 SGD, total_charged 4.50 SGD, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the whole contested 4.50 SGD returns to the rider. To the driver: your reading of POL-NS-10(f) as the governing charging rule is rejected. Limb (f) charges 'a rider's own cancellation after the grace in limb (a) or (b)' — that is, one falling after the free-cancellation period has run. This cancellation was made inside the limb (b) advance grace (17:35:08, before the window opened at 17:40:08), so limb (f) is not engaged and limb (b) governs. Your remaining points are accepted as correct on the record but do not change the outcome: the driver did begin navigating 8 seconds after acceptance (17:10:16), the trace runs 157 fixes with no gaps and 100% coverage, no limb (f) refund exception is made out, and the 4.50 SGD fare line reconciles to the platform's published figure, so no POL-NS-08(d) defect arises. To the rider: your core case is right, and it is independently supported. The baseline no-show charge also fails: POL-NS-01 limb (a) requires a driver 'arrived' event in the trip record and there is none (arrived_at is null and the event list runs driver_assigned to driver_en_route to trip_cancelled only), and limb (d) requires termination under RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT, whereas the record closes with RIDER_CANCELLED. The driver's own trace places him about 14,000 m from the pickup pin and moving at 57–63 km/h at the moment of cancellation, so the 180-second free waiting period was never served (0 seconds of in-geofence dwell) and POL-NS-06 supports a full refund. No driver compensation is payable: POL-NS-01 is not satisfied on any limb, so POL-NS-07's payout condition is never reached, and the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip (no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the required 4, and 2/90 = 0.022, below the required 0.08), so POL-NS-09(d) is not engaged. Evidence quality: the ruling rests on the trip record and the fare breakdown, both carrying weight_multiplier 1.0, and no POL-NS-08 limb is engaged (no clock skew, no trace gap over 120 seconds, the chat log is internally consistent, and the fare line reconciles), so confidence is not capped below 1.0 and is stated at 0.92. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02738-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; it carries no fact this ruling needs (POL-NS-06(i) accumulation is not required) and it does not affect the outcome or the confidence. No clause produces a referral and the case does not escalate: confidence 0.92 is above the 0.70 floor. The monetary effect of 4.50 SGD is at or below the 8.00 SGD execution threshold, so this provisional ruling is executed automatically on issue.
